certificate.title: Treat AI Like Staff: Using Agentic AI Tools Effectively Completion

course.description: Learn how to use agentic AI tools the way you'd delegate to a capable staff member — with planning, clear instructions, and proper review.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Treat AI Like Staff: Using Agentic AI Tools Effectively.

activities.title: Stop treating AI like a chat window

lessons.content: The biggest mistake people make with agentic tools is typing questions like it's a search engine. Instead, frame your request as a work assignment: "Here are the source files. Here's what I need. Here's the format." Give it a task, not a question.
lessons.title: Stop treating AI like a chat window

lessons.content: Before handing work to an AI agent, outline what you want: What are the inputs? What does the final deliverable look like? What format should it be in? Skipping this step leads to mediocre outputs and wasted iterations.
lessons.title: Plan before you execute

activities.title: Build durable instructions instead of repeating yourself

lessons.content: If you find yourself giving the same instructions across sessions, write them into a reusable instruction file or skill. This is the equivalent of creating an SOP for a new hire — do it once, benefit every time.
lessons.title: Build durable instructions instead of repeating yourself

activities.title: Match the reasoning level to the task

lessons.content: Not every task needs the most powerful model. Use high-reasoning models (like Opus) for complex multi-step analysis. Use faster models (like Sonnet) for formatting, drafting, and routine tasks. Using the wrong reasoning level wastes time or produces inaccurate output.
lessons.title: Match the reasoning level to the task

activities.title: Always review the output — polished doesn't mean correct

lessons.content: AI outputs look professional by default. That's dangerous. Review every deliverable the same way you'd review work from a junior staff member. Check the logic, verify the numbers, and confirm the conclusions follow from the data.
lessons.title: Always review the output — polished doesn't mean correct

activities.title: Don't try to automate unstable processes

lessons.content: If your current workflow is messy, inconsistent, or undocumented, AI will amplify the mess. Fix the process first, then automate. AI works best when it's replicating a well-defined, repeatable workflow.
lessons.title: Don't try to automate unstable processes

lessons.content: Your first attempt will rarely be perfect. Refine your instructions, add examples of good output, and correct mistakes. Most people quit before they've learned how to work with the tool effectively. Give it 3-5 serious attempts before judging the tool.
lessons.title: Iterate instead of giving up
